Celine: FYI vendor HundredCloud charged 23% VAT on SaaS invoice to Redwood IE entity. Invoice HC-2026-778 shows EUR 8,000 + EUR 1,840 VAT. PO 77022. PDF: https://invoices.example.com/HC-2026-778.pdf

Omar: Is the invoice billed to Redwood IE (we have IE VAT 987654321) on the PO? If so, this should be reverse-charged (B2B cross-border). Vendor charged UK VAT by mistake.

Celine: PO billed to Redwood EU Ltd (Ireland). PO includes IE VAT 987654321. Vendor's VAT on invoice shows GB123456789. I attached both PO screenshot and vendor invoice.

Vik: TaxOps note: For intra-EU B2B supplies, supplier should not charge VAT when buyer provides a valid VAT ID; buyer self-assesses via reverse charge. If vendor charged VAT and we haven't paid yet, request reissue net referencing our IE VAT. If payment already made, reclaim via EU refund procedure (slow) or ask vendor to issue credit.

AP: Placed a hold on payment and emailed vendor: "Please reissue net invoice referencing IE VAT 987654321 or provide written explanation for VAT charged."

Vendor (email quoted): "Apologies, they used the GB billing template. We'll reissue a net invoice and send by tomorrow." :white_check_mark:

Celine: For audit, save original invoice + vendor note + reissued invoice. If they insist on VAT charged, we need their VAT registration evidence and then decide refund vs input VAT claim.

invoice-bot: Event: invoice_hold placed (invoice=HC-2026-778, reason=vat_charged_intra_eu)

Omar: Also add a short-term automation: when PO has a customer VAT ID, flag vendor invoice VAT country mismatch and auto-place hold. Cuts manual triage.

Vik: Agreed. Long-term: vendor onboarding should include mandatory country-prefix validation for VAT IDs. If vendor delays >48h, AP to request credit memo and tax ops to prepare EU refund route. Tagging @AP to follow-up in 24h.

Celine: I'll monitor vendor reissue. Thanks everyone.
